sentences.text: Theriosuchus is an extinct genus of basal crocodilian known from the Early Cretaceous of Asia and England.
It was a common terrestrial basal crocodilian in Europe during the Cretaceous period.
Theriosuchus was one of the few basal crocodilians present in Laurasia during the Late Cretaceous.
Scientists have recorded 44 fossil occurrences of this animal in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus Theriosuchus was first described by Richard Owen in 1879.
The Paleobiology Database lists the genus name as Theriosuchus, attributed to Owen in 1878.
Theriosuchus is classified within the family Atoposauridae.
Three valid species of Theriosuchus are recognized: T. pusillus from southern England, T. grandinaris from Thailand, and T. morrisonensis from North America.
A 2016 analysis suggests Theriosuchus is a neosuchian related to Paralligatoridae rather than Atoposauridae.
The species T. ibericus and T. symplesiodon were moved from Theriosuchus to the genus Sabresuchus.
The species T. guimarotae was reassigned from Theriosuchus to the genus Knoetschkesuchus.
The genus authority for Theriosuchus is Owen, 1879.
The time range for Theriosuchus is estimated from 168.6 to 66 million years ago.
Fossils of Theriosuchus date from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous periods.
Theriosuchus lived in Europe, Southeast Asia, and western North America during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.
Fragmentary records of Theriosuchus exist from the Middle Jurassic and Early Cretaceous in China, Morocco, and Scotland.
